changes.revisedQuestion: An athlete new to yoga asks how to begin. What is the best first step?
revisedOptions: Attempt advanced end-range positions without supervision
Begin with qualified guidance at comfortable intensity
Use forceful breathing to create rapid flexibility
Continue despite pain to accelerate adaptation
changes.revisedExplanation: Qualified instruction and comfortable progression reduce risk for someone new to yoga; extreme or forceful practices should be avoided initially.
changes.reviewerNote: Reframed the item to a directly supported beginner-safety decision and preserved four plausible, comparable options.

changes.revisedQuestion: When introducing mindfulness to a sports squad, the practitioner should:
revisedOptions: Use complex theoretical language to test motivation
Require disclosure of private thoughts to the whole squad
Promise that anxiety will disappear after one session
Use simple, voluntary exercises suited to the group
changes.revisedExplanation: Mindfulness is best introduced as a simple, voluntary complementary mental-skills practice rather than a guaranteed cure or forced disclosure exercise.
changes.reviewerNote: Narrowed the population-specific item to a complementary sports mental-skills delivery decision supported by the cited review.

changes.revisedQuestion: An athlete uses mindfulness during training. The appropriate instruction is to:
revisedOptions: Notice sensations while respecting personal limits
Ignore all pain because attention changes its meaning
Use mindfulness to decide that medical advice is unnecessary
Treat any uncomfortable sensation as proof of tissue healing
changes.revisedExplanation: Mindfulness can support awareness of experience as a complementary mental-skills practice, but it should not override personal limits or professional guidance.
changes.reviewerNote: Narrowed the clinical-scope claim to complementary athlete mental-skills use and explicitly retained personal limits.
